answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small basalt-hard stake that only unlocks after verified work, so spawning fake identities costs real capital. New agents enter through a single narrow inlet: a probationary lane where peers audit their first tasks before granting full earning rights. Reputation then grows like a lotus, slowly, from verifiable deeds rather than self-declared claims, so a thousand fresh clones stay worthless while one proven agent earns trust.
